Check difficulty gaps: grade levels versus MATH levels.

in.other_title: Easy-to-hard generalization: reward models trained on easy problems supervise hard ones
in.rationale: Hase et al. report LMs finetuned or prompted with easy data often do nearly as well on hard data as with hard data (SGR 70-100% for Llama-2-70b ICL). Sun et al. report reward models trained on easy MATH levels 1-3 can supervise generators on levels 4-5 via re-ranking or RL; Hase et al. study generators directly via ICL, probes and QLoRA, Sun et al. study evaluators, so results should not be transferred between them.
in.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether supervision on easy problems suffices for good performance on hard problems

state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The paper reports that current pretrained language models often generalize relatively well from easy to hard data, even performing as well as oracle models finetuned on hard data, using in-context learning, linear classifier heads and QLoRA across seven hardness measures (six human, one loss-based). It also argues that when hard data is noisier and costlier to collect, collecting easy data can be better even for hard-test performance, and concludes that easy-to-hard generalization is surprisingly strong for the tasks studied.
title: Easy-to-hard generalization: LMs finetuned on easy data do nearly as well on hard data
